barriers.studentWording: I cannot work out what the words mean
barriers.immediateSupport: Play the audio once more, then read only the line they name. Paraphrase that one line in plain English beside the original — never instead of it.
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Model one line, compare meanings, then return to the poet's wording. Hold the framing: dialect is a creative choice, not an error.
barriers.solves: Stops the learner reading dialect as a mistake, or giving up on page one.

barriers.studentWording: I do not know what to write
barriers.immediateSupport: Listen once more and capture ONE word only. Use a single stem: 'One word that stays with me is…'. Accept it spoken or drawn.
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Lower the bar out loud — one word is a complete answer at this stage. Do not ask for a sentence yet.
barriers.solves: Breaks initial inertia without demanding written fluency.

barriers.studentWording: It goes too fast, or I cannot hear it properly
barriers.immediateSupport: Switch to the source text alongside the audio, or use the transcript. Pause and replay as often as needed — there is no listening limit.
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Check it is a pace need, not a device fault. If no sound at all, route to technical support instead.
barriers.solves: Separates a genuine access need from a broken speaker.

barriers.studentWording: I can read it but I do not know what it feels like
barriers.immediateSupport: Replay the audio, then name three mood words only. Do not explain them yet.
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Ask for tone, rhythm and emotional effect separately. Three words is the whole task.
barriers.solves: Moves the learner from literal reading to emotional understanding.

barriers.studentWording: I do not know what the poem is actually about
barriers.immediateSupport: Answer one question in one sentence: what is this poem asking me to notice? That sentence becomes the core-meaning statement.
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Hold the approval gate here. Do not let generation begin without an approved core-meaning statement.
barriers.solves: Protects Stage 3 from unfocused prompting and wasted generation.

barriers.studentWording: Both poems feel the same to me
barriers.immediateSupport: Put the two atmosphere maps side by side and find one word that could only belong to one poem.
resources: 2.2 Atmosphere Map — Bang Wata Come Yah!!
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Sameness here usually means Stage 2 was rushed. Ask what is different about the two atmospheres before allowing Stage 3.
barriers.solves: Prevents two identical-looking poem pages later in the book.

barriers.type: Meaning will not become a prompt
barriers.studentWording: I know what it means but I cannot turn it into an image
barriers.immediateSupport: Open the Prompt Builder and fill ONE part only: Subject. Then stop and check it against the poem before adding Setting.
resources: Six-Part Prompt Structure (Subject · Setting · Action · Mood · Style & Lighting · Avoid)
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Narrow the task to one part at a time. Check each choice traces back to a line in the poem.
barriers.solves: Converts interpretation into action without overwhelming.

barriers.studentWording: Can I just paste the poem in?
barriers.immediateSupport: No — the AI cannot read a poem the way you can. Name the one line driving your image, then build the prompt from that line.
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Show the failure case: pasted poem produces whimsical nonsense. Hold the golden rule — analyse, then decide the prompt.
barriers.solves: Protects fidelity and stops surface-word generation.

barriers.studentWording: The AI keeps giving me the wrong thing
barriers.immediateSupport: Change ONE part of the six only, then regenerate. Record what changed in the Evidence Log.
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Enforce one-variable edits. Random regeneration teaches nothing and burns time.
barriers.solves: Builds cause-and-effect understanding of prompting.

barriers.studentWording: I like more than one image and do not know which fits
barriers.immediateSupport: Compare only two at a time, and ask one question of each: which stays truer to the poem?
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Redirect from 'prettiest' to 'truest'. Require a pointer back to a line.
barriers.solves: Supports justified choice rather than preference alone.

barriers.studentWording: None of these images feel right
barriers.immediateSupport: That is a real finding, not a failure. Note it in the Evidence Log and return to Stage 3 to revise one prompt part.
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Affirm the judgement, then send them back to Stage 3. Do not let a weak image get locked into the build.
barriers.solves: Prevents a poor image being carried into assembly.

barriers.studentWording: I chose it because I liked it
barriers.immediateSupport: Finish this sentence instead: 'This image is true to the poem because the line ___ says ___.' Spoken is fine.
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Require the poem pointer. Accept it spoken if writing is the barrier.
barriers.solves: Turns taste into evidence-based reasoning.

barriers.studentWording: There is too much on the page
barriers.immediateSupport: Keep only three visible elements in the first pass: poem, image, audio. Add nothing else until those sit right.
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Point to the exact next area to fill. Remove anything non-essential before adding.
barriers.solves: Reduces overload and unblocks the commonest Stage 5 stall.

barriers.studentWording: My poem has gone into one block and lost its lines
barriers.immediateSupport: Paste as plain text, then re-break the lines by hand against the source. Never leave poetry reflowed as prose.
resources: BC_S1_Source_Text (Volcano Action / Bang Wata Come Yah!!)
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Check this at Stage 5, not Stage 6. Line integrity is a fidelity issue, not a cosmetic one.
barriers.solves: Protects the poet's line breaks, stanza spacing and voice.

barriers.studentWording: I do not know what to do first
barriers.immediateSupport: Build one page at a time in this order: poem text, then image, then audio, then title.
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Sign off the assembly plan before building starts. This prevents rebuilds.
barriers.solves: Gives a finite, ordered path through an open-ended task.

barriers.studentWording: I am finished but I cannot explain why I did it this way
barriers.immediateSupport: Use one stem per element: 'I chose this image because…', 'I chose this audio because…'. Say it out loud and record it.
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Ask for brief explanation, not an essay. Spoken reflection counts fully.
barriers.solves: Supports concise reflection and publish readiness.

barriers.studentWording: I do not know what to say about using AI
triggers: do i say i used ai
barriers.immediateSupport: State three things: what you decided, what the AI produced, what you changed afterwards.
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Frame disclosure as authorship evidence, not confession. Use the 40/20/40 split as the structure.
barriers.solves: Makes ethical authorship concrete and non-threatening.

barriers.studentWording: My link does not work / nobody can open my book
barriers.immediateSupport: Test the published link yourself in a private window before submitting.
barriers.lecturerIntervention: This is a technical fault, not a learning barrier — route to support, then re-test.
barriers.solves: Separates system friction from pedagogical friction.

barriers.studentWording: I can read the poem but the point is unclear
barriers.immediateSupport: Read the poem, then open the inspiration note beside it. The concern behind the poem is the point.
resources: Room 1 Hotspot Copy & Link Map — Current (HS1, HS2)
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Explain the human issue behind the poem before any design talk begins.
barriers.solves: Anchors Room 1 in meaning rather than novelty.

barriers.studentWording: I do not know where to click or what to look at first
barriers.immediateSupport: Start at the hotspot nearest the centre and work outward. You only need HS1 before moving on.
resources: Room 1 Hotspot Copy & Link Map — Current
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Name the first hotspot out loud. Spatial disorientation is a design problem, not a comprehension one.
barriers.solves: Solves the ThingLink-specific problem that has no Book Creator equivalent.

barriers.studentWording: It goes too fast, or I cannot hear it properly
barriers.immediateSupport: Open the captions or transcript hotspot and follow the text while it plays.
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Check whether it is a pace need or a device fault before intervening.
barriers.solves: Separates a genuine access need from a broken speaker.

barriers.studentWording: I can see the image but I do not know why it fits
barriers.immediateSupport: Replay the audio and read the symbolism note at the same time. Ask what is close and what is far away.
resources: TL Room 2 HS1, HS2 (music reasoning + hero image symbolism notes)
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Model the link between sound, image and emotional distance explicitly.
barriers.solves: Helps learners who can see an image but not read it.

barriers.studentWording: I do not understand why that music was chosen
barriers.immediateSupport: Listen once with eyes closed, then name what the music does that the words do not.
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Point out that soothing music can still carry distance. Tone is a decision, not decoration.
barriers.solves: Connects auditory intent to emotional meaning.

barriers.studentWording: The 360 view is too much for me
barriers.immediateSupport: Stop moving the view. Stay on one still section and use the text hotspots instead.
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Offer the flat/text route as an equal path, not a lesser one. Do not require 360 navigation.
barriers.solves: Removes a genuine access barrier unique to immersive platforms.

barriers.studentWording: I do not know what to put in the prompt
barriers.immediateSupport: One scene, one mood, one symbol. Nothing else goes in this prompt.
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Reduce to a single-scene brief. A whole story will not render as one image.
barriers.solves: Prevents overcrowded, incoherent prompt writing.

barriers.studentWording: Can I just paste the poem in?
barriers.immediateSupport: No — name the one line driving your image, then build the prompt from that line.
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Show the failure case, then return to the keyword bank.
barriers.solves: Protects fidelity and stops surface-word generation.

barriers.studentWording: I cannot find the right words from the poem
barriers.immediateSupport: Pull five words only: what you see, hear, and feel. Stop at five.
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Model reading-to-keyword transfer on one stanza, then hand it back.
barriers.solves: Gives a concrete first step when prompting feels abstract.

barriers.studentWording: I just picked the nicest image
barriers.immediateSupport: Put your choice beside one you rejected and name what is gained and what is lost.
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Ask what emotional or symbolic detail changes between the two options.
barriers.solves: Improves image judgement and justification.

barriers.studentWording: I do not know how to say why I rejected one
barriers.immediateSupport: Say what the image added that the poem never asked for. That is your reason.
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Model rejection as fidelity work, not failure.
barriers.solves: Makes rejection a reasoned, teachable act.

barriers.studentWording: None of these images feel right
barriers.immediateSupport: That is a real finding. Return to Room 3 and change one prompt part only.
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Affirm the judgement, then route back to Room 3.
barriers.solves: Prevents a weak image entering the assembled room.

barriers.studentWording: There are too many hotspots and I do not know the order
barriers.immediateSupport: Place only the first three hotspots, in the order a visitor should meet them. Nothing else yet.
resources: Hotspot map (in ThingLink Hotspot Copy — Rooms 2–6)
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Point to hotspot one, then two, then three. Sequence before quantity.
barriers.solves: Solves the main Unit 5 assembly problem in ThingLink.

barriers.studentWording: I do not know what should go in one hotspot
barriers.immediateSupport: One hotspot answers one question. If it answers two, split it.
resources: TL Room 5 HS2 media package by hotspot
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Check coherence inside a single hotspot before looking at the whole room.
barriers.solves: Stops hotspots becoming dumping grounds.

barriers.type: Media will not place or play
barriers.studentWording: My image or audio will not load into the hotspot
barriers.immediateSupport: Check the file size and format first, then re-add the media to the hotspot.
barriers.lecturerIntervention: This is a technical fault — route to support rather than teaching into it.
barriers.solves: Separates system friction from pedagogical friction.

barriers.studentWording: I am not sure this is ready to publish
barriers.immediateSupport: Run the audit checklist rather than guessing. If every line passes, it is ready.
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Use the checklist as sign-off. Replace 'does it feel done' with 'does it pass'.
barriers.solves: Supports confident final publication.

barriers.studentWording: I do not know what to say in my reflection
barriers.immediateSupport: One sentence per choice: image, sound, order. Record it spoken if that is easier.
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Brief and specific beats long and general. Spoken reflection counts fully.
barriers.solves: Makes reflection finite and achievable.

barriers.studentWording: My share link does not work
barriers.immediateSupport: Test the published link yourself in a private window before submitting.
barriers.lecturerIntervention: Technical fault — route to support, then re-test the link.
barriers.solves: Separates system friction from pedagogical friction.
